h1: IntelligentX — AI & SaaS Hero Section Design
tagline: Hero section reference built on white #EDEEF5 and bright lime #9FFF00, set in Inter and measured against 110vh sections.
summary: Hero section reference for an AI or SaaS product — React and Tailwind CSS, #9FFF00 accent, a 640x462 frame and Inter.
about: IntelligentX was captured at 640x462 and kept as a specification rather than as a gallery image. The colour scheme is white #EDEEF5 underneath, black #1A1A1A for the type and bright lime #9FFF00 carrying the accents, and the page is set in Inter. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 640x462 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Keep it open while you write: the 4,182-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: Links before the action
layout.body: Navigation is a thin strip rather than a band: wordmark left, links centre-right, one #9FFF00 action, all of it sitting above the hero section without a background of its own. The links are set below the wordmark in size, and the #9FFF00 action is the only element in the bar with any weight.

layout.title: Values you can check
layout.body: Sizes are quoted rather than inherited: 110vh sections and 16px spacing steps. Swap the face or the copy and those relationships still hold. The brief states values rather than proportions, so the composition keeps its relationships when the copy changes length.

layout.title: Display size does the talking
layout.body: The type is Inter at the top of the scale, with the supporting copy dropped well below it so the hierarchy needs no colour to read. Tracking is set per size, so the display line and the caption do not share one letter-spacing value. Keep the size steps even if you change the face.

layout.title: The nav is deliberately thin
layout.body: The bar sits over the 640x462 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

motion.title: Static by design
motion.body: This one is delivered as a still composition at 640x462, so the hierarchy has to work without motion, and it does. Motion is treated as feedback rather than as decoration.

motion.title: Motion that stays out of the way
motion.body: Only the elements that respond to the pointer move. No scroll timelines needed.

editorial.title: The order behind the hero section
editorial.body: Read it in order: navigation, the announcement badge, the stats row, the form and the background clip. Each element has one job, and the bright lime #9FFF00 accent is spent only on the element you are meant to press. A SaaS reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: What to change first in IntelligentX
editorial.body: Compare this with starting from a blank page. Here the frame (640x462) and 110vh sections and 16px spacing steps are already decided, so the work is substitution rather than composition. A different brand can reuse the whole frame.

editorial.title: Why the SaaS brief holds
editorial.body: Where a template fills the fold with modules, this hero section uses navigation, the announcement badge, the stats row, the form and the background clip and stops. The difference shows in 110vh sections and 16px spacing steps: nothing is padded to fill space. It gives a SaaS reader the shortest honest route to the offer.

faq.question: Is the IntelligentX prompt a finished spec or a starting point?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 4,182 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: How much of IntelligentX depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: IntelligentX was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: How should I handle the IntelligentX media in a client build?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 640x462.
